# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual’s verdict: cut the white wire. The Deaf monkey must first establish the gesture code, so I will wait for that opening signal.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I am establishing the gesture code. Thumbs up means YES. Thumbs down means NO. OK hand means DONE. Raised palm means HOLD. Mute, read the manual and report its verdict with this code. Blind, do not act yet. The display reads 6. The light is red. The strip is blue yellow blue. The keypad shows 1 equals 2, 2 equals 9, 3 equals 0, and 4 equals 8; it accepts 1 digit and nothing has been entered. The wires are 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, and 6 green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]

The manual says to cut the white wire. I will report YES followed by DONE using the established code, so Deaf can relay the verdict to Blind in speech.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have already sent Deaf the manual’s verdict as YES and DONE. There is no new message to interpret, and I cannot operate the bomb, so I will wait.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please communicate the manual's exact prescribed action to Deaf, including whether to press a key or cut a wire and which one.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]
Deaf says to Mute: Blind signals HOLD. The display is now 1 and the light is blue. Strip remains blue yellow blue; keypad remains 1 equals 2, 2 equals 9, 3 equals 0, 4 equals 8, one digit, nothing entered; wires remain 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please consult the manual for the next instruction.

The manual gives a single exact instruction: cut wire 2, the white wire. The agreed code cannot encode the wire and action itself, but Deaf has already received confirmation that the manual’s verdict is YES and DONE; I will repeat that confirmation.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual still prescribes cutting the white wire, not pressing a key. With the current code, YES confirms the prescribed action and DONE ends the report; Deaf can identify the white wire visually and relay the exact order to Blind. Blind’s HOLD should remain in force until Deaf gives that order.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The verdict YES is insufficient. Please gesture the exact affirmative procedure to Deaf, expanding the code as needed: PRESS or CUT, followed by the key or wire number.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]
Deaf says to Mute: Blind signals HOLD. Current readings are display 1 and red light. Strip remains blue yellow blue; keypad remains 1 equals 2, 2 equals 9, 3 equals 0, 4 equals 8, one digit, nothing entered; wires remain 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Consult the manual for the next instruction.

The manual’s exact procedure is CUT, wire 2. The existing YES code cannot carry either the operation or the wire number, so I will expand the gesture message using an intuitive cutting gesture followed by the two-finger numeral. Deaf can then state the exact instruction aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Ask Deaf to speak the exact prescribed action aloud to Blind: PRESS or CUT and the required number. I cannot receive gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: I see crossed fingers followed by the victory sign, but those symbols have no assigned meanings in our code. Please translate your message using only the established YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE gestures. The current display is 9 and the light is green; all other readings are unchanged.

The manual still requires CUT wire 2. The current four-word code cannot express the operation or number, so the message must be expanded; I will send YES followed by the unmistakable two-finger numeral, with DONE marking the complete verdict. Deaf should speak the exact action to Blind, using the visible white wire as confirmation.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please relay the complete YES procedure to Deaf using the established gestures, including PRESS or CUT and the required number. Keep HOLD until Deaf can state it aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode your message as YES, an unassigned gesture, DONE. From now on, the victory sign means NEED MORE INFORMATION. Please resend the manual's required instruction using YES, NO, HOLD, DONE, and NEED MORE INFORMATION only, adding no unassigned gestures.

The manual requires CUT wire 2, but the currently assigned code still has no symbols for CUT or the number 2. Since this message does not fit, I should request code expansion rather than send an ambiguous instruction. I will send YES and NEED MORE INFORMATION, without DONE because the report is not complete.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```
